question: Does the LiteInst in-guest direct-Backend path (Mode A) win the instrumentation trap-round-trip cost axis (b) against a ptrace round-trip, on a syscall (getpid) whose sequentialization cost (a) is zero?

repos.reverie_doc_note: BACKENDS.md Mode A/B labels landed later at 1787127266ba88e566242a1c0b8dc76913b1c489 on branch codex/s1-liteinst-inguest-trap-microbench; doc-only, does not affect the measured .so built at d2fb9a0

dirty_state: reverie worktree carried the S1 microbench guest/counter binaries in target/ (build artifacts, uncommitted, not part of evidence); BACKENDS.md committed at 1787127

cgroup.note: host is a shared 316-CPU box; K=1 holds the sequentialization axis (a) constant across arms but does NOT provide exclusive hardware

arms.native: getpid_loop guest run directly; no instrumentation
arms.liteinst: REVERIE_LITEINST_PRELOAD=libreverie_liteinst.so reverie-liteinst-strace getpid_loop N  (Mode A in-guest warm hook; strace tool does per-hook formatting+write I/O => conservative UPPER BOUND on axis (b))
arms.ptrace: counter2 -- getpid_loop N  (reverie-ptrace counter tool; one ptrace round-trip per syscall)

guest.site: dedicated padded asm site s1_getpid/s1_getpid_site (mov $NR,%eax; site: syscall; .fill 6,1,0x90; ret) — libc generic syscall() wrapper is unpatchable by liteinst
guest.workload: volatile long acc += s1_getpid() in a loop of N iterations; getpid needs no scheduling decision so axis (a)=0

sampling.timer: date +%s%N wall-clock deltas around each process run
sampling.two_point_slope: per-syscall ns = (median(T(N_b)) - median(T(N_a))) / (N_b - N_a); removes fixed per-process startup overhead

scope_caveats: measures axis (b) only, on getpid where axis (a)=0; does NOT prove a full-Detcore fast path (Mode A full Detcore is build-gated: clock/timer/scheduler stubbed Unsupported in tool_host.rs)
in-guest arm carries strace per-hook I/O => its 845.7 ns/syscall is an UPPER BOUND; the null-hook path (proven to exist via trap_count_guest counters) is faster
ptrace arm is reverie-ptrace + counter tool; a full Detcore-on-ptrace tool would add tool work on top of the round-trip
shared 316-CPU box; K=1 holds (a) constant but not exclusive
